featured.title: Hormuz Traffic Falls to Four Recorded Vessels as Alternative Oil Routes Come Under Focus
featured.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world's most closely watched shipping routes. Preliminary tracking data recorded only four vessel crossings on Tuesday, compared with a 10-day average of 18. None of the recorded vessels was a very large crude carrier or LNG tanker, although some ships may have travelled with transponders switched off. Saudi Arabia is meanwhile offering additional crude shipments through Oman's Sohar port as it seeks to reduce the impact of disruption to its East-West pipeline. Oil prices have eased slightly, but the wider fuel market remains tight.

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Remains Severely Restricted
articles.content: Preliminary tracking data shows only four recorded vessel crossings through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, well below the recent 10-day average of 18. Two vessels entered and two exited, and none was a very large crude carrier or LNG tanker. Analysts caution that tracking systems may not capture ships travelling with their transponders disabled.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Turns to Oman as Alternative Crude Route
articles.content: Saudi Arabia is offering additional crude cargoes through Oman's Sohar port following disruption to its East-West pipeline. The alternative route is being used to reduce pressure on Saudi export logistics while the damaged infrastructure remains affected.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia Oman Sohar oil port tanker

articles.title: Oil Prices Ease but Diesel Market Remains Tight
articles.content: Brent crude was around $108.16 per barrel while U.S. WTI traded around $104.63 during Wednesday trading. Prices eased as additional Saudi supply through Oman reduced some immediate supply concerns. However, European diesel prices remain close to record levels and U.S. diesel has moved above $6 per gallon.
articles.imageQuery: oil price market barrels crude oil

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Strengthens Its Position in Global Fuel Markets
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery has become an increasingly important supplier to international fuel markets during the disruption to Middle Eastern supplies. The refinery recorded $1.82 billion in net profit during the first half of 2026 on revenue exceeding $13 billion. Reuters reported that Dangote supplied significant volumes of jet fuel to Europe during the second quarter, while diesel and gasoil exports also increased.

articles.title: Dangote IPO Remains a Major Nigerian Business Story
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals is offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each in an IPO targeting approximately ₦2.15 trillion, or about $1.6 billion. The offer is scheduled to close on 13 October 2026. The minimum subscription is 10 shares, with the proceeds intended partly to support expansion of refining capacity towards 1.4 million barrels per day.

articles.title: EU Opens Door to Closer Partnership With Canada
articles.content: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed opening the way for Canada to become the European Union's first associate member. The proposal would focus on closer cooperation in areas including defence, energy, technology, raw materials and supply chains. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was present in Strasbourg for the European Parliament address. Any such arrangement would require agreement from EU member states.

articles.title: Brussels Signals Tougher Approach to China Trade Imbalance
articles.content: The European Commission says it will use available measures to address what it considers an unsustainable trade deficit with China. The issue comes as European manufacturers face growing competition from Chinese companies across several industrial sectors. Brussels is also seeking stronger European access to critical raw materials and more resilient supply chains.
articles.imageQuery: EU China trade flags cargo containers

articles.title: Russian Drone Strikes Kill Five Civilians in Southern Ukraine
articles.content: Ukrainian officials say Russian drone strikes in southern Ukraine killed five civilians and injured seven others. A passenger bus was struck near Nikopol. A separate passenger train in the Mykolaiv region was also attacked, but all 168 passengers and crew were evacuated safely. Russia had not immediately commented on the reported attacks.

articles.title: EU Plans Talks With Leading AI Companies Over Safety
articles.content: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU will invite leading frontier AI laboratories for discussions about testing, verification and the risks associated with increasingly powerful artificial-intelligence systems. The initiative comes amid growing debate over how quickly advanced AI should be developed and how safety measures should keep pace.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence technology Europe AI computer

articles.title: Senegal and IMF Signal Progress Towards New Support Programme
articles.content: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva have welcomed progress in discussions aimed at establishing a new IMF-supported programme. Talks are focusing on economic recovery, debt sustainability, investment and employment as Senegal works to strengthen its public finances.
articles.imageQuery: Senegal President Bassirou Diomaye Faye IMF meeting

articles.title: Asian Markets Remain Cautious as Investors Watch Oil and U.S. Rates
articles.content: Asian markets remain sensitive to movements in oil prices, shipping disruptions and expectations around U.S. monetary policy. Investors are assessing whether elevated energy costs could keep inflation pressures high while central banks consider their next policy decisions.
articles.imageQuery: Asian stock market financial district screens

articles.title: Global Fuel Costs Remain a Major Economic Concern
articles.content: The energy disruption is increasingly affecting refined fuels rather than crude alone. European diesel remains near record levels, while the U.S. national diesel average has moved above $6 per gallon. Higher fuel costs can feed into transport, aviation, manufacturing, food distribution and household expenses if the disruption persists.

morningSummary: Good afternoon. The global energy crisis remains the dominant international story. Hormuz recorded only four vessels on Tuesday, far below its recent average, while Saudi Arabia is seeking alternative crude routes through Oman. Brent remains above $108 and U.S. WTI above $104, although prices have eased slightly. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery is supplying growing volumes of fuel to international markets while its major IPO continues. Europe is also strengthening its relationship with Canada, reviewing its trade imbalance with China and increasing attention on advanced AI safety. Ukraine remains under heavy drone attacks, while Senegal is pursuing a new IMF-supported economic programme.
bigQuestion: If oil prices remain above $100 while shipping routes stay under pressure, how much longer can businesses absorb the extra costs before consumers feel the impact?
